data: Is the value of the black square, representing the CST method, always higher than the value of the red circle for '8gram' when comparing construction memory for 16 GB input size?

The question asks whether the value of the black square, representing the CST method, is always higher than the value of the red circle for '8gram' when comparing construction memory for 16 GB input size. 

From the analysis of the graph:

1. The black square represents the CST method, and the red circle represents the KenLM method for '8gram'.
2. At an input size of 16 GB, the black square (CST) is consistently above the red circle (KenLM) on the y-axis, which represents memory [GiB].
3. This trend is observed across all the data points for the 16 GB input size.

Therefore, the value of the black square, representing the CST method, is indeed always higher than the value of the red circle for '8gram' when comparing construction memory for 16 GB input size.
